summary: Two brothers married to two sisters died. The remaining brothers may not do yibum with either sister, because each is the sister of a woman tied to them, so they do chalitzah.

chunks.en: Four brothers,
chunks.st: In the case of four brothers,

chunks.en: two of them were married to two sisters,
chunks.st: two of whom were married to two sisters,

chunks.en: and the ones married to the sisters died.
chunks.st: and the ones married to the sisters died,

chunks.en: These sisters do chalitzah, but not yibum.
chunks.explain: Each sister is tied to the brothers, so her sister is forbidden like a wife's sister.
chunks.st: then those sisters must perform ḥalitza and may not enter into levirate marriage.
chunks.stMore: Since both sisters require levirate marriage with each of the surviving brothers, a levirate bond exists between each sister and the brothers. Each of them is considered the sister of a woman with whom each brother has a levirate bond and is therefore forbidden to him by rabbinic law.

chunks.en: And if they went ahead and married them,
chunks.st: And if they married the sisters before consulting the court,

chunks.en: they must send them away. Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: they should divorce them, for the Sages decreed that in this situation they may not remain married. Rabbi Eliezer says that there is a dispute in this matter:

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say they may stay married,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say: He may maintain her as his wife,

chunks.en: and Beis Hillel say they must send them away.
chunks.st: while Beit Hillel say: They must divorce them.

summary: If one sister is a forbidden relative to one brother, that brother may do yibum with the other sister. But a smaller prohibition does not help, and she does only chalitzah.

chunks.en: If one of them was forbidden
chunks.st: If one of the sisters was forbidden

chunks.en: to one brother as a forbidden relative,
chunks.st: to one of the brothers due to a prohibition against forbidden relations because she was a relative of his wife or a relative on his mother’s side, then

chunks.en: he may not marry her, but he may marry her sister.
chunks.st: he is forbidden to marry her but permitted to marry her sister.
chunks.stMore: Because she is his close relative, she is exempt from levirate marriage with him, and therefore she is not bound to him with a levirate bond. Consequently, her sister is not considered the sister of a woman with whom he has a levirate bond, and he is permitted to enter into levirate marriage with her.

chunks.en: But the second brother is forbidden to both of them. If an issur
chunks.st: But the second brother, who is not a close relative of either sister, is forbidden to marry both of them. Indeed, for him each woman remains the sister of a woman with whom he has a levirate bond. If a prohibition resulting from

chunks.en: mitzvah or issur kedushah is the problem,
chunks.st: a mitzva or a prohibition stemming from sanctity will be transgressed when one of the women marries one of the brothers, then her sister must

chunks.en: she does chalitzah, but not yibum.
chunks.st: perform ḥalitza and may not enter into levirate marriage, as she is considered the sister of a woman with whom he has a levirate bond.
chunks.stMore: In this case, the sister who is forbidden to the brother due to a mitzva or due to sanctity is bound to the brother for the purpose of ḥalitza.

summary: If each sister is a forbidden relative to a different brother, each brother may do yibum or chalitzah with the sister who is not his relative.

chunks.en: If one of them was forbidden
chunks.st: If one of those women was forbidden

chunks.en: to this brother as a forbidden relative,
chunks.st: to this one brother due to a prohibition against forbidden relations

chunks.he: וְהַשְּׁנִיָּה אֲסוּרָה עַל זֶה אִסּוּר עֶרְוָה,
chunks.en: and the second was forbidden to that brother as a forbidden relative,
chunks.st: and the second woman was forbidden to that second brother due to a prohibition against forbidden relations,

chunks.en: the one forbidden to this one is allowed to that one,
chunks.st: then she who is forbidden to this brother is permitted to that brother,

chunks.en: and the one forbidden to that one is allowed to this one.
chunks.st: and she who is forbidden to that brother is permitted to this one.

chunks.en: This is what they meant when they said,
chunks.st: And this is the case that was referred to when they said:

chunks.en: "If her sister is also her yevamah,
chunks.st: When her sister is also her yevama, i.e., in a case where two sisters are also yevamot and therefore happened for levirate marriage before two brothers,

chunks.en: she either does chalitzah or yibum."
chunks.st: she either performs ḥalitza or enters into levirate marriage.
chunks.stMore: This must be referring to a case where each sister is forbidden to one of the brothers due to a prohibition concerning forbidden relatives. In this case, each sister has a levirate bond only with the one brother to whom she is permitted, and the prohibition against marrying the sister of a woman with whom one has a levirate bond does not apply. Therefore, each brother can either perform the act of ḥalitza or consummate the levirate marriage with the sister to whom he is not related.

summary: If two brothers were married to two close relatives, like sisters or a mother and daughter, and both died, the third brother does chalitzah but not yibum. Rabbi Shimon frees them completely.

chunks.en: Three brothers,
chunks.st: In the case of three brothers,

chunks.en: two of them were married to two sisters,
chunks.st: two of whom were married to close relatives, e.g., two sisters;

chunks.en: or a woman and her daughter,
chunks.st: or a woman and her daughter;

chunks.en: or a woman and her daughter's daughter,
chunks.st: or a woman and her daughter’s daughter;

chunks.en: or a woman and her son's daughter.
chunks.st: or a woman and her son’s daughter, if the two brothers who were married to two close relatives died and their wives happened before a third brother for levirate marriage,

chunks.en: These do chalitzah, but not yibum.
chunks.st: then these two women must perform ḥalitza and may not enter into levirate marriage, as each of them is a relative of a woman with whom he has a levirate bond.

chunks.en: And Rabbi Shimon frees them.
chunks.st: And Rabbi Shimon exempts them even from the obligation to perform ḥalitza.

chunks.en: If one of them was forbidden
chunks.st: If one of them was forbidden

chunks.en: to him as a forbidden relative,
chunks.st: to him, the third brother, due to a prohibition against forbidden relatives, then

chunks.en: he may not marry her, but he may marry her sister.
chunks.st: he is prohibited from marrying her but is permitted to marry her sister.
chunks.stMore: Because the woman who is forbidden to him is not considered to be a woman who requires him for levirate marriage, there is only one woman who happens before him for levirate marriage.

chunks.en: If it is an issur mitzvah or an issur kedushah,
chunks.st: However, if one of the women was forbidden due to a prohibition resulting from a mitzva or a prohibition stemming from sanctity, then

chunks.en: they do chalitzah, but not yibum.
chunks.st: they must perform ḥalitza and may not enter into levirate marriage. This is because these prohibitions do not completely cancel the levirate bond.

summary: The single brother made a maamar with one sister, and then the other sister also fell to him. Beis Shammai let him keep the first; Beis Hillel say he loses both, so "woe to him" for both.

chunks.en: Three brothers,
chunks.st: In the case of three brothers,

chunks.en: two of them were married to two sisters,
chunks.st: two of whom were married to two sisters,

chunks.en: and one was single.
chunks.st: and one who was single, the following occurred:

chunks.en: One of the sisters' husbands died,
chunks.st: The husband of one of the sisters died childless, leaving behind his wife,

chunks.en: and the single brother made a maamar with her.
chunks.st: and the single brother performed levirate betrothal [ma’amar] to this wife.
chunks.stMore: The single brother performed an act of betrothal to the yevama but did not yet consummate the marriage by engaging in sexual intercourse.

chunks.en: After that, his second brother died.
chunks.st: Afterward, the second brother died, and therefore the second brother’s wife, the sister of the betrothed, happened before the single brother for levirate marriage as well.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: In this case, Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: "His wife stays with him,
chunks.st: His wife remains with him. The woman he betrothed is considered like his wife, and he is not required to divorce her.

chunks.en: and the other one goes out because she is his wife's sister."
chunks.st: And this other woman leaves the yavam and is exempt from levirate marriage as the sister of a wife.

chunks.en: But Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: Beit Hillel say:
chunks.stMore: Being as he had not yet entered into marriage with the first woman, he is required to perform levirate marriage with both women. Therefore,

chunks.en: "He sends away his wife with a get and chalitzah,
chunks.st: he divorces his wife, i.e., the woman to whom he performed levirate betrothal, with a bill of divorce, which nullifies levirate betrothal, and by ḥalitza, which nullifies the levirate bond.

chunks.en: and his brother's wife with chalitzah."
chunks.st: And, he sends away the wife of his second brother with ḥalitza as well.

chunks.en: This is what they said:
chunks.st: They comment: This is the case that was referred to when the Sages said:

chunks.en: "Woe to him for his wife, and woe
chunks.st: Woe unto him for his wife and woe unto him

chunks.en: to him for his brother's wife."
chunks.st: for the wife of his brother. Due to the combination of circumstances, he loses them both.

summary: A brother did yibum with his sister-in-law and then died. The last brother is married to her sister, so she is freed, and the other wife is freed as her co-wife. After only a maamar, the other wife does chalitzah.

chunks.en: Three brothers,
chunks.st: In the case of three brothers,

chunks.en: two of them were married to two sisters,
chunks.st: two of whom were married to two sisters

chunks.en: and one was married to an unrelated woman.
chunks.st: and one who was married to an unrelated woman, the following occurred:

chunks.en: One of the sisters' husbands died,
chunks.st: The husband of one of the sisters died childless,

chunks.en: and the one married to the unrelated woman married his wife,
chunks.st: and the brother who was married to the unrelated woman married, i.e., performed lev irate marriage with, the deceased brother’s wife

chunks.he: וָמֵת, הָרִאשׁוֹנָה יוֹצְאָה מִשּׁוּם אֲחוֹת אִשָּׁה,
chunks.en: and then he died. The first goes out because she is his wife's sister,
chunks.st: and later died himself, childless. In this situation, both women happen for levirate marriage before the other, remaining, brother. The first woman is dismissed due to the prohibition proscribing the sister of one’s wife, as she is the sister of this brother’s wife,

chunks.en: and the second goes out because she is her co-wife.
chunks.st: and the second woman is dismissed due to her status as the first woman’s rival wife.
chunks.stMore: Following the first levirate marriage, this second woman became the rival wife of the sister, and is therefore exempt from levirate marriage as well.

chunks.en: If he only made a maamar with her
chunks.st: If, however, the brother married to the unrelated woman performed only levirate betrothal, but had not yet consummated the levirate marriage with the sister,

chunks.en: and died, the unrelated woman does chalitzah, but not yibum.

chunks.en: and then he died. The first goes out because she is his wife's sister,

summary: A woman who was forbidden to a brother even for a short time stays forbidden to him forever. But a relative who was divorced before the husband died does not free her co-wife.

chunks.en: Three brothers,
chunks.st: In the case of three brothers,

chunks.en: two of them were married to two sisters,
chunks.st: two of whom were married to two sisters

chunks.en: and one was married to an unrelated woman.
chunks.st: and one who was married to an unrelated woman, the following occurred:

chunks.en: One of the sisters' husbands died,
chunks.st: One of the husbands of the sisters died,

chunks.en: and the one married to the unrelated woman married his wife.
chunks.st: and he who was married to the unrelated woman married the deceased husband’s wife,

chunks.en: Then the second brother's wife died,
chunks.st: and then the wife of the second brother, the other one of the sisters, died.

chunks.en: and after that the one married to the unrelated woman died.
chunks.st: Afterward, the brother who was married to the unrelated woman died, leaving two women for levirate marriage before the remaining brother:
chunks.stMore: The unrelated woman and the woman who was previously prohibited as the sister of his deceased wife.

chunks.en: She is forbidden to him forever,
chunks.st: In this case, the sister is forbidden to him forever.
chunks.stMore: She is not forbidden due to her status as his wife’s sister, as his wife already died and one’s wife’s sister is permitted after the wife’s death. However,

chunks.en: because she was forbidden to him for one moment.
chunks.explain: When she first fell to him, she was his wife's sister.
chunks.st: since she was already forbidden to him at one time, she is forbidden to him forever.
chunks.stMore: When she first happened before the brothers for levirate marriage, before the third brother married her, she was forbidden to the second brother as his wife’s sister. Therefore, she is forbidden to him forever. In addition, she exempts her rival wife, the unrelated woman, from levirate marriage.

chunks.en: Three brothers,
chunks.st: In the case of three brothers,

chunks.en: two of them were married to two sisters,
chunks.st: two of whom were married to two sisters

chunks.en: and one was married to an unrelated woman.
chunks.st: and one who was married to an unrelated woman, the following occurred:

chunks.he: גֵּרֵשׁ אֶחָד מִבַּעֲלֵי אֲחָיוֹת אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ,
chunks.en: One of the sisters' husbands divorced his wife,
chunks.st: Shimon, the husband of one of the sisters, divorced his wife, and then Levi,

chunks.en: and the one married to the unrelated woman died,
chunks.st: who was married to the unrelated woman, died, and

chunks.en: and the one who had divorced married her,
chunks.st: Shimon, the man who divorced his wife, married, i.e., performed levirate marriage with, her, i.e., this unrelated woman.

chunks.en: and then he died. This is what they said,
chunks.explain: Now the last brother may do yibum with the unrelated woman.
chunks.st: And then Shimon himself later died, so that the unrelated woman happened for levirate marriage before Reuven, the third brother, who is married to the second sister. In this scenario, Reuven is allowed to consummate the levirate marriage with the unrelated woman. This is the case that was referred to when they said:

chunks.en: "And all of them who died or were divorced,
chunks.st: And with regard to all those fifteen forbidden relatives who died or were divorced,

chunks.en: their co-wives are allowed."
chunks.st: their rival wives are permitted to enter into levirate marriage.
chunks.stMore: This is because at the time that they happened before the yavam for levirate marriage they were no longer the rival wives of a forbidden relative.

summary: If it is not sure whether a forbidden relative was really married or really divorced, her co-wife must do chalitzah but not yibum. The mishnah gives examples of such doubtful kiddushin and doubtful gittin.

chunks.en: And any of them who had kiddushin
chunks.st: And if any of these fifteen women who are prohibited as forbidden relatives

chunks.en: or a get that was in doubt,
chunks.st: had undergone a betrothal or divorce whose status is uncertain with the deceased brother,

chunks.en: their co-wives
chunks.st: then those women who were their rival wives must

chunks.en: do chalitzah, but not yibum.
chunks.st: perform ḥalitza and may not enter into levirate marriage since they are possibly the rival wives of forbidden relatives.

chunks.en: How can kiddushin be in doubt?
chunks.st: The mishna elaborates: How could there be a situation of uncertainty with regard to betrothal? If in the public domain

chunks.en: If he threw her the kiddushin,
chunks.explain: He threw her a ring or coin across a street.
chunks.st: he threw her an item for the purpose of betrothal and there were eight cubits between them, and the item

chunks.he: סָפֵק קָרוֹב לוֹ סָפֵק קָרוֹב לָהּ,
chunks.en: and it may have landed nearer to him or nearer to her,
chunks.st: was possibly closer to him and did not enter into her domain, and possibly closer to her, i.e., within four cubits of her, whereby she could acquire the object,

chunks.en: that is a doubtful kiddushin.
chunks.st: this is a case of uncertainty with regard to betrothal.

chunks.en: A doubtful get:
chunks.st: Uncertainty with regard to divorce occurs when, for instance,

chunks.he: כָּתַב בִּכְתַב יָדוֹ וְאֵין עָלָיו עֵדִים,
chunks.en: he wrote it in his own handwriting, but no witnesses signed it,
chunks.st: he wrote a bill of divorce in his handwriting but there are no signatures of witnesses on the document,

chunks.he: יֵשׁ עָלָיו עֵדִים וְאֵין בּוֹ זְמָן,
chunks.en: or witnesses signed, but there is no date in it,
chunks.st: or there are the signatures of witnesses on the document but there is no date written in it,

chunks.en: or there is a date, but there is
chunks.st: or the date is written in it but there is only

chunks.en: only one witness,
chunks.st: the signature of a single witness.
chunks.stMore: Since there is doubt as to whether these three kinds of bills of divorce are valid, a woman who was divorced through them is only possibly divorced, and so

chunks.en: that is a doubtful get.
chunks.st: this case is called uncertainty with regard to divorce.

summary: A widow tied to two brothers at once (from her husband and from a maamar) cannot do yibum, because the Torah speaks of one yavam. The mishnah also repeats: a woman forbidden for one moment stays forbidden forever.

chunks.en: Three brothers married to three unrelated women,
chunks.st: In the case of three brothers who were married to three unrelated women,

chunks.en: and one of them died,
chunks.st: and one of the brothers died, the following occurred:

chunks.en: and the second made a maamar with her,
chunks.st: The second brother performed levirate betrothal with the wife of the deceased brother and before he was able to consummate the levirate marriage

chunks.he: וָמֵת, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ חוֹלְצוֹת וְלֹא מִתְיַבְּמוֹת,
chunks.en: and he died. These do chalitzah, but not yibum,
chunks.st: he died as well, leaving behind two women who happen before the third brother for levirate marriage. Then those two women must perform ḥalitza and may not enter into levirate marriage.

chunks.en: as it says (Devarim 25),
chunks.st: As it is stated: “If brothers dwell together

chunks.he: וּמֵת אַחַד מֵהֶם יְבָמָהּ יָבֹא עָלֶיהָ,
chunks.en: "and one of them dies… her yavam shall marry her,"
chunks.st: and one of them dies and he has no child, the wife of the dead man shall not be married outside of the family to one not of his kin; her brother-in-law will have intercourse with her” (Deuteronomy 25:5). This teaches that a woman eligible for levirate marriage is one

chunks.en: someone tied to one yavam,
chunks.st: who has one levirate relationship

chunks.en: and not someone tied to two yevamim.
chunks.st: and not one who has a double levirate relationship.
chunks.stMore: In this case, the wife of the first deceased brother requires levirate marriage due to both the marriage with her first husband as well as the levirate betrothal with the second brother.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says: He may

chunks.en: He does yibum with whichever one he wants,
chunks.st: consummate the levirate marriage with whichever woman he wishes and then

chunks.en: and does chalitzah with the second.
chunks.st: perform ḥalitza with the second.

chunks.en: Two brothers married to two sisters,
chunks.st: In the case where two brothers were married to two sisters,

chunks.en: and one of them died,
chunks.st: and one of the brothers died, the widow at this point would be exempt from levirate marriage as the sister of his wife.

chunks.he: וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵתָה אִשְׁתּוֹ שֶׁל שֵׁנִי,
chunks.en: and after that the second brother's wife died.
chunks.st: And afterward the wife of the second brother died. Although the yevama is no longer the sister of his wife,

chunks.en: She is forbidden to him forever,
chunks.st: this woman is nevertheless forbidden to him forever,

chunks.en: because she was forbidden to him for one moment.
chunks.st: since she had already been forbidden to him at one time.

summary: Two grooms were mixed up at their weddings, and each went home with the wrong bride. This is a serious sin, and the mishnah teaches what must be done afterward.

chunks.en: Two men made kiddushin with two women,
chunks.st: In the case of two men who betrothed two women,

chunks.en: and when they went in to the chuppah, they switched
chunks.st: and at the time that they entered the wedding canopy, after the betrothal, the men

chunks.en: this one's bride to that one,
chunks.st: switched this wife with that wife

chunks.en: and that one's bride to this one.
chunks.st: and that one with this one,

chunks.he: הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ חַיָּבִים מִשּׁוּם אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ.
chunks.en: They are guilty of the sin of a married woman.
chunks.st: then these two men are liable for engaging in forbidden sexual relations with a married woman, since each of them had intercourse with his fellow’s wife.
chunks.stMore: The act of betrothal is sufficient to prohibit a woman to all other men as a married woman. Therefore, when the women were switched, both men transgressed this violation.

chunks.en: If they were brothers,
chunks.st: And if they were brothers, then they are also liable

chunks.en: also for a brother's wife.
chunks.st: for forbidden sexual relations with a brother’s wife.

chunks.en: And if they were sisters,
chunks.st: And if these women were sisters,

chunks.en: also for a woman and her sister.
chunks.st: then they are liable for taking a wife and her sister as well.

chunks.en: And if they were niddah,
chunks.st: And if they were menstruating women,

words.note: A woman who is tamei in a certain way.

chunks.en: also because of niddah.
chunks.st: they would be liable for intercourse with a menstruating woman as well.

chunks.en: And we keep them apart for three months,
chunks.st: And following these forbidden sexual relations, we separate these women from their husbands for three months,

chunks.en: in case they are expecting a baby.
chunks.st: lest they were impregnated by that forbidden act of intercourse.
chunks.stMore: Doing so makes it possible to distinguish a child born of these relations, so that he could be rendered a mamzer.

chunks.he: וְאִם הָיוּ קְטַנּוֹת שֶׁאֵינָן רְאוּיוֹת לֵילֵד,
chunks.en: If they were young girls who cannot have children yet,
chunks.st: And if they were female minors and unable to bear children,

chunks.en: we give them back right away.
chunks.st: then we immediately return them to their original husbands.

chunks.en: And if they were from Kohen families,
chunks.st: And if they were daughters of priests,

chunks.en: they may no longer eat terumah.
chunks.st: they are thereby disqualified from eating of teruma. By engaging in illicit sexual acts, they were rendered forbidden to priests and disqualified from eating teruma.

words.note: A gift of food for Kohanim.
